item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00477","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C13","C19","C23"],"selected_candidate_label":"C13","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C13 is the clear drafting parent. The child expressly identifies the September 9, 1957 tung-oil proclamation and incorporates its quota periods and quota amounts into a new combined tung-oil/tung-nut restriction. It also repeats C13's product-specific statutory findings, representative period, entry terminology, and equitable-treatment concern. The child therefore does more than resemble C13: it extends C13's operative quota machinery to tung nuts through an oil-equivalency formula. C19 is a weaker structural analogue because it combines related products under one aggregate quota and supplies product-conversion rules. C23 closely parallels the standard recital sequence and aggregate-quota mechanism, but its common language is less distinctive and largely reflects recurring section 22 drafting.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Whereas, on September 9, 1957, I issued [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] ... limiting the quantity of tung oil that may be entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption during the periods specified in that proclamation","parent_excerpt":"That for the period commencing September 9, 1957 ... the total quantity of tung oil entered shall not exceed 26,000,000 pounds ... [with further quota periods and limits]","explanation":"The child expressly invokes C13 and uses its existing tung-oil quota periods and quantities as the framework for the new restriction."},{"child_excerpt":"no tung nuts shall be permitted to be entered ... after the total aggregate quantity of tung nuts and tung oil ... has reached, in terms of oil, the equivalent of the quota for tung oil specified in that proclamation for such quota period","parent_excerpt":"That for the period commencing September 9, 1957 ... [and subsequent specified periods], the total quantity of tung oil entered shall not exceed 26,000,000 pounds","explanation":"The child's central operative provision adapts C13's tung-oil quotas into a combined quota covering tung oil and the oil equivalent of tung nuts."},{"child_excerpt":"the price-support program ... with respect to tung nuts and tung oil ... products processed in the United States from domestic tung nuts or tung oil","parent_excerpt":"the price-support program undertaken by the Department of Agriculture with respect to tung nuts and tung oil ... products processed in the United States from domestic tung nuts or tung oil","explanation":"The product-specific description of the protected program and domestic processing is substantially the same."},{"child_excerpt":"the representative period from November 1, 1952, to October 31, 1956, inclusive","parent_excerpt":"the representative period November 1, 1952 to October 31, 1956, inclusive","explanation":"Both rely on the identical product-specific representative period for the statutory 50-percent finding."},{"child_excerpt":"For the purposes of this proclamation the oil content of tung nuts shall be computed on the basis of 15.9 pounds for each 100 pounds of whole nuts, and ... 35.8 pounds of oil for each 100 pounds of decorticated nuts.","parent_excerpt":"the total quantity of tung oil entered shall not exceed 26,000,000 pounds","explanation":"The conversion formula is the new administrative mechanism that makes tung nuts commensurable with, and thus governed by, C13's existing oil-denominated quotas."}]}
